brands.name: Saltwater Café
brands.excerpt: A seaside café that takes coffee seriously and itself not at all.
brands.content: Saltwater is a twelve-table café on the Fort Kochi waterfront. I’ve worked with them since their opening week — on positioning, social, menus and the occasional chalkboard pun.

brands.name: Ledgerly
brands.excerpt: A personal-finance app for people who’d rather not think about personal finance.
brands.content: Ledgerly helps first-time earners track, save and stop panicking. My job: make money talk sound less like a lecture and more like a friend who’s good with numbers.

brands.name: Monsoon Threads
brands.excerpt: Handloom-inspired everyday wear, made for wet weather and warm people.
brands.content: Monsoon Threads makes quick-dry clothing with a handloom soul. I wrote their brand voice book, launch campaigns and most of the words on their swing tags.

brands.name: Bright Path Academy
brands.excerpt: Online learning for curious kids — and their slightly less curious parents.
brands.content: Bright Path runs live online classes for school students. I rewrote their website, course pages and admissions emails, and wrote their back-to-school print campaign.

brands.name: Coastline Realty
brands.excerpt: Homes along the Kerala coast, sold without the jargon.
brands.content: Coastline Realty sells homes to first-time buyers who are tired of being talked down to. I write their guides, listings and print advertising — all in plain English.

brands.name: Tiny Tusk Toys
brands.excerpt: Wooden toys with big personalities, made in small batches.
brands.content: Tiny Tusk started as a weekend workshop and is now a small, much-loved toy brand. I named it, wrote its voice, and still write its social posts.

works.title: How UPI Actually Works — Explained for First-Timers
works.excerpt: A 1,800-word explainer that turns a 40-step process into one cup of chai’s worth of reading.
works.brief: Ledgerly’s support inbox was full of the same question: “Where does my money go between pressing Pay and the shop getting it?” They needed one piece of content that answered it once and for all.
works.idea: Explain UPI like a relay race — your bank, the switch, their bank — with one runner per paragraph and zero acronyms left undefined. Every section ends with a single “in short” line for skimmers.
works.result: Became the app’s most-read help article within a month, ranks on page one for “how does UPI work”, and cut related support tickets by roughly a third.

works.title: The Plain-English Guide to Buying Your First Home
works.excerpt: A buyer’s guide that swaps “encumbrance certificate” anxiety for a calm, step-by-step checklist.
works.brief: First-time buyers were dropping off halfway through Coastline’s website — overwhelmed by legal terms nobody had explained to them.
works.idea: A 12-step guide written like a conversation with a patient elder sibling. Every legal term gets a one-line translation and a “why it matters” note, and the whole thing ends with a printable checklist.
works.result: The guide is now the first thing every Coastline agent sends to new leads, and the checklist PDF is downloaded more than any listing brochure.

works.title: Course Pages That Parents Actually Finish Reading
works.excerpt: Rewrote 24 course pages to answer the three questions every parent asks — in the first ten seconds.
works.brief: Bright Path’s course pages were written for teachers, not the parents paying for them. Long syllabi, short on reasons.
works.idea: Every page now opens with the same three answers: What will my child be able to do? How much time does it take? Why this, why now? The syllabus moved below the fold, where curious parents still find it.
works.result: Enquiries from course pages rose noticeably in the first term after launch, and the same structure is now the template for every new course.

works.title: Monday Called. We Sent Coffee.
works.excerpt: A Monday-morning social series that turned the worst day of the week into the café’s busiest.
works.brief: Saltwater was packed on weekends and painfully quiet on Mondays.
works.idea: Own Monday. A weekly post that treats Monday like a difficult relative — and cold brew as the only reasonable response.
works.result: Monday footfall grew week on week through the series, and regulars started quoting the posts back at the counter.

ig.caption:
Monday called. We let it go to voicemail. ☕

New cold brew on tap at Saltwater, Fort Kochi. Bring your worst Monday — we’ll fix it in one sip.

#SaltwaterCafe #MondayMood #ColdBrew #FortKochi

works.title: Rain Check? Never.
works.excerpt: Launch posts for a rain-proof handloom collection — written to be read under an umbrella.
works.brief: Launch the Monsoon Edit, a quick-dry handloom range, in the one season fashion brands usually avoid.
works.idea: Flip the season: the rain isn’t a problem, it’s the point. Short, splashy lines that sound like a friend daring you to step outside.
works.result: The launch post became the brand’s most-shared post of the year, and the first drop sold through ahead of plan.

ig.caption:
Some brands fear the rain. We designed for it. 🌧️

The Monsoon Edit is here — quick-dry handloom that looks good soaked.

#MonsoonThreads #RainReady #Handloom #SlowFashion

works.title: Screen Time, Meet Tree Time.
works.excerpt: Always-on social copy for a wooden-toy brand that would rather you put your phone down.
works.brief: Sell wooden toys on the one platform designed to keep children (and parents) on screens.
works.idea: Be honest about the irony. A gentle, funny series that nudges parents to log off — with a toy in hand.
works.result: Comments filled with parents tagging each other, and the series became the brand’s signature tone on social.

ig.caption:
Screen time, meet tree time. 🐘

Every Tiny Tusk toy is carved from responsibly sourced wood and comes with zero batteries and infinite stories.

#TinyTuskToys #WoodenToys #PlayMore @tinytusk.toys

works.title: #ChaiWithStrangers — A Pop-up That Got Kochi Talking
works.excerpt: One long table, forty strangers, zero phones. A café pop-up that earned press coverage and a waiting list.
works.brief: Make a small café famous without a big budget.
works.idea: Once a month, Saltwater sets one long table for forty strangers. Phones go in a basket; conversation cards go on the table. The press release was written as an invitation, not an announcement.
works.result: Featured in local newspapers and city guides, sold out every month since launch, with a waiting list for the next table.

works.title: Money Talks — Ledgerly’s College Roadshow
works.excerpt: A ten-campus roadshow where students roasted their own spending habits — live, on stage.
works.brief: Introduce a finance app to students who think budgeting is something their parents do.
works.idea: A stand-up style show where volunteers read out their last ten UPI transactions and the host (and the crowd) roasts them — then shows how the app would have helped.
works.result: Ten campuses, packed auditoriums, and clips that travelled far beyond the venues.

works.title: The Rain Walk — Monsoon Threads Launch
works.excerpt: A runway, but outdoors, in the pouring rain. The press release practically wrote itself.
works.brief: Launch a rain-proof collection in a way nobody could ignore.
works.idea: Hold the fashion show outside, during the monsoon, with no backup plan. Guests got umbrellas; models got none.
works.result: Covered across fashion and lifestyle press, and the event photos became the campaign imagery for the season.

works.title: Your Landlord Will Miss You.
works.excerpt: Full-page launch ad for a first-home buyers’ scheme — with a headline renters couldn’t scroll past.
works.brief: Announce a low-down-payment scheme to people who’d given up on owning a home.
works.idea: Speak to the renter, not the buyer. A headline with a wink, and body copy that does the maths for them.
works.result: The scheme’s launch weekend brought in more site visits than the previous quarter combined.

img.headline: Your landlord will miss you.
img.sub: Own a home on the coast with a down payment smaller than a year’s rent. Coastline’s First Home scheme does the paperwork, the maths and the worrying — you just pick the view.

works.title: Fees? We Left Them at the Last Bank.
works.excerpt: Front-page jacket for a zero-fee account launch.
works.brief: Launch a zero-fee savings account with a single newspaper jacket.
works.idea: Make the absence of fees the hero — a headline that sounds like a breakup note to your old bank.
works.result: The jacket drove a sharp spike in app installs on launch day, and the line was picked up across social.

img.headline: Fees? We left them at the last bank.
img.sub: No minimum balance. No hidden charges. No small print you need a lawyer for. Ledgerly’s new account is free — and we’ve made it boringly easy to keep it that way.

works.title: Ask More Questions. Get Better Answers.
works.excerpt: Back-to-school ad celebrating the most annoying (and most important) word: why.
works.brief: A back-to-school print ad that stands apart from discount-heavy coaching ads.
works.idea: Celebrate the child who keeps asking “why?” — and position Bright Path as the place that keeps answering.
works.result: Admissions for the new term filled faster than the year before, and parents quoted the headline in enquiry calls.

img.headline: Ask more questions. Get better answers.
img.sub: Every great scientist, writer and inventor was once a child who wouldn’t stop asking why. At Bright Path, we never tell them to stop. Admissions open for the new term.

works.title: Tiny Tusk Toys — Naming, Voice & Tagline
works.excerpt: From 212 name options to one small elephant with a big personality.
works.brief: A weekend woodworking hobby was becoming a business, and it needed a name, a voice and a reason to exist.
works.idea: An elephant — big-hearted, gentle, remembers everything — made tiny. The voice became warm and a little cheeky: the favourite uncle of toy brands. Tagline: “Small toys. Big stories.”
works.result: The name and voice now carry everything from packaging to social, and customers describe the brand in the same words we wrote.

works.title: Monsoon Threads — The Brand Voice Book
works.excerpt: A 30-page voice guide that taught a fashion brand to talk like a friend with good taste.
works.brief: Five people were writing for the brand, and it sounded like five different brands.
works.idea: A voice book built around one idea — “warm, wet and witty” — with do/don’t pairs, word lists and before/after rewrites for every channel.
works.result: The whole team writes from the same playbook now, and new hires are onboarded with the book on day one.

works.title: Saltwater Café — Positioning & Identity Words
works.excerpt: “Serious coffee. Unserious people.” — the line that became a menu, a mural and a mood.
works.brief: A new café on a street full of cafés needed a reason to be remembered.
works.idea: Be precise about the coffee and playful about everything else. The positioning line led to menu names, chalkboard rules and a mural on the front wall.
works.result: The line is now painted on the wall, printed on the cups and quoted by regulars — the clearest sign a positioning worked.
